statement: Let $A$ be any small category, $\widehat A=\operatorname{Set}^{A^{\op}}$, and $i_A X=A/X$ its category of elements. For a fundamental localizer $W$ put $W_A=i_A^{-1}W$. For each $S\in\widehat A$ there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \widehat A/S\cong\operatorname{Set}^{(A/S)^{\op}}. \] There are two specified, weakly saturated classes on this slice obtained from B.1: \[ W^{\mathrm{pre,el}}_S=i_A^{-1}W^{\mathrm{pre}}_{A/S},\qquad W^{\mathrm{co,el}}_S=i_A^{-1}W^{\mathrm{co}}_{A/S}. \] Both are contained in the total class $W_A$ over $S$. These define localizations for any $A$, but test-category theory alone does not identify them with the two simplicial theories of Part~B.
notes: Two specified elements-based candidates, not an unstated unique notion.

statement: Assume $W\subseteq W_0$. For every small $A$ and $S\in\widehat A$, $W^{\mathrm{pre,el}}_S$ consists exactly of isomorphisms. For $A=\Delta$, $S=1$, and $W=W_\infty$, $W^{\mathrm{co,el}}_1$ is instead the ordinary class of weak homotopy equivalences of simplicial sets. Their enhanced localizations are not equivalent. Thus transporting both fine tests through the category of elements does not give an automatic extension of Part~B to presheaves.
notes: Candidate duality fails already on the test category Delta; does not deny directed simplicial opposition.

statement: Define a map $u:X\to Y$ in $\widehat A$ to be elementwise $W$-smooth or $W$-proper when $i_Au:A/X\to A/Y$ has that categorical property. Every presheaf map is elementwise $W$-smooth, for every fundamental localizer. If $W\subseteq W_0$, a map is elementwise $W$-proper exactly when all its naturality squares are pullbacks of sets. Already for the test category $A=\Delta$, no autoequivalence of $\widehat A$ can exchange these two classes.
notes: All maps elementwise smooth; proper iff naturality squares cartesian for W subset W0.

statement: Let $M$ have pullbacks and a weakly saturated class $W$, and let $\mathcal L_+,\mathcal L_-$ be two pullback-stable classes. Suppose $D:M\to M$ is an involutive equivalence preserving $W$, together with its canonical pullback comparisons, and carrying $\mathcal L_+$ to $\mathcal L_-$. Then the universal-test classes satisfy \[ D(W_S^{\mathcal L_+})=W_{DS}^{\mathcal L_-}, \] and $D$ induces an equivalence of the corresponding enhanced slice localizations. It also exchanges their universal raw-pullback-preserving classes. Such data are sufficient; being a test category supplies none of the required exchange isomorphisms by itself.
notes: Exact sufficient duality data; changing index to its opposite is distinct from simplex reversal.

statement: For $1\leq n\leq\omega$, write $V^{(n)}$ for strict $n$-functors whose Street nerves are weak homotopy equivalences; this notation is distinct from the truncation localizer $W_n$ of B.10. Use the under-slices of \citet[\S4]{BCAraMaltsiniotis2018} and their total-dual over-slices. For a strictly commuting triangle $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\to S$, either of the conditions \[ s\backslash u\in V^{(n)}\quad(s\in S_0), \qquad\text{or}\qquad u/s\in V^{(n)}\quad(s\in S_0) \] implies $u\in V^{(n)}$. The same result allows the specified oplax triangle in the cited theorem.
notes: Opened exact Theorem A references and slice conventions; independent of model claim.

statement: For a strict small $n$-category $S$, define $V^{\mathrm{pre}}_S$ and $V^{\mathrm{co}}_S$ by the two slice tests in C.5. They are weakly saturated and contained in the total class $V^{(n)}$. Let $D_{\mathrm{tot}}$ reverse every positive-dimensional cell. Then \[ (n\Cat/S,V^{\mathrm{pre}}_S) \cong(n\Cat/D_{\mathrm{tot}}S,V^{\mathrm{co}}_{D_{\mathrm{tot}}S}) \] as relative categories, and hence their enhanced localizations are equivalent. This conclusion holds for every $1\leq n\leq\omega$ and uses none of the claimed September 2026 model structures.
notes: Formal fine duality for every strict dimension, with total-cell reversal.

statement: For each subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, or $J\subseteq\mathbb N_{>0}$ when $n=\omega$, reversing the $j$-cells for $j\in J$ defines an involutive automorphism $D_J$ of strict $n$-categories and preserves $V^{(n)}$. The generators commute and compose by symmetric difference. Define $\Liss^{(n)}$ to be the maps whose every strict base change preserves $V^{\mathrm{co}}$ under raw pullback, and $\Prop^{(n)}$ using $V^{\mathrm{pre}}$. Then both classes contain isomorphisms and are stable under composition and strict base change; $D_{\mathrm{tot}}$ exchanges them. These definitions alone do not identify them with a higher lifting-category criterion or with smooth/proper Street-nerve maps.
notes: All cell dualities and universal preservation definitions; no unproved lifting characterization.

statement: The category of strict $2$-categories has the proper combinatorial Thomason model structure with weak equivalences detected by the Street nerve, and $c_2\operatorname{Sd}^2\dashv\operatorname{Ex}^2N_2$ is a Quillen equivalence with simplicial sets in the Kan--Quillen structure.
notes: Verified published dimension-two theorem, not reliance on September 2026 claim.

statement: Suppose, for a fixed $n$, that the model structure and Quillen equivalence claimed in family~317 are valid. Then the total-weak-equivalence localization of $n\Cat/S$ presents $\Spaces_{/BN_nS}$, the slice of spaces over the classifying space of the Street nerve. It has the usual derived postcomposition and pullback adjunctions. This is a coarse statement. It does not imply recognition of C.6's fine localizations or any universal base-change property for the classes in C.7. For $n=2$ the premise is already verified by C.8.
depends_on: C.8 for n=2; conditional OpenAI2026Thomason for n>2

statement: For a general strict $n$-category $S$, $2\leq n\leq\omega$, the following specific extension is not proved here: the Street nerve induces equivalences from the two enhanced localizations in C.6 to the actual covariant and contravariant localizations over $N_nS$, with the slice conventions matched as in C.5; moreover C.7's preservation classes admit a local higher comma-lifting criterion and satisfy the universal Kan base-change axioms of Part~E. These are required before declaring every such $(n\Cat,V^{(n)},\Liss^{(n)},\Prop^{(n)})$ an instance of the abstract theorem. Accepting family~317 does not remove these requirements.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Recent-results family 317; Parts C and E
notes: Open relative Street-nerve recognition and higher base-change criterion; exact missing comparisons stated.
